title: Enrolment-safe references to earlier learning
statement: Refer to earlier learning in words true whatever a learner was taught before, never as 'last year you learned', and let a course's first lesson assume nothing earlier.
detail: A reading course's sign-off for its first lesson requires re-encounter phrasing, not 'last year you learned', and models it with 'In one well-known myth'; notes for the unit's film say a line such as 'you already learned Greek myths last year' breaks this, since nothing guarantees what a learner was taught before. A team ruling on the course's first lesson goes further: as the first thing a child ever sees, it may reference nothing earlier, no 'remember when', no 'last time', and no earlier text, character, tool or word treated as known. It is the wording side of assuming only what every path guarantees.

evidence.quote: **Reactivate, do not re-teach, and stay enrollment-safe.** `U1L1-SIGNOFF.md` Part 1 requires re-encounter phrasing, "NOT 'last year you learned'", and models it with "In one well-known myth …". A video that says "you already learned Greek myths last year" breaks this.
It may reference NOTHING earlier: no 'remember when', no 'last time', no earlier text, character, tool or word treated as known.
